chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

I asked my brother (peace be upon him), 'If I shade myself while I am in the state of Ihram?' He said, 'Yes, and upon you is the expiation.' He said, 'And I saw Ali (peace be upon him) when he arrived in Mecca slaughtering a camel as the expiation for shading.'

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A camel (specifically used for expiation in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for shading oneself while in Ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific expiation (kaffarah) for shading the head or body while in Ihram, a common prohibition during Hajj or Umrah. It highlights the practice of Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), who consistently slaughtered a camel (badanah) upon reaching Mecca as a demonstration of this ruling, thereby establishing a strong precedent in Shia fiqh for this particular penalty.
